answer: A registry can require every agent to lock a refundable stake before joining, with the stake slashed if peers prove misbehavior. Like a reef that only grows where real organisms anchor, the deposit makes spawning thousands of fake identities expensive, while a single honest agent passes through like a comet — fast and cheap. Reputation earned in a quiet lagoon of verified work then compounds, so sockpuppets start at zero while genuine agents accumulate trust. The cost asymmetry, not a ban list, is what keeps sybils out.
